homeLocation.title: Villa Ballena & Villa Beluga — relaxed Mediterranean elegance in Svetvinčenat, Istria
homeLocation.p1: Villa Ballena and Villa Beluga sit on a quiet country road in Svetvinčenat, the medieval village at the green heart of Istria, Croatia. From the front gate it is a 300-metre walk to the village square, the konoba, and the 13th-century Kaštel Morosini-Grimani — and only 33 km to Pula Airport, 23 km to Rovinj, and 19 km to the nearest Adriatic beach at Bale.
homeLocation.p2: Each villa is a 350 m² private luxury retreat: four en-suite bedrooms, a heated 8 × 4 m biological pool, a Finnish sauna or full game room, and a kitchen built around an induction hob, ice maker, and capsule coffee machine. Both villas were built in 2021, share a clay tennis court, and accept up to two pets at no extra charge.
homeLocation.p3: Booked together as Complex BeBa, Villa Ballena and Villa Beluga sleep up to 18 guests with two pools, two kitchens, and one combined property — the format Croatian families and international groups choose for weddings, milestone birthdays, and corporate retreats.
homeLocation.p4: Ballena & Beluga is the rare Istria address that combines designer interiors with small-village authenticity. From the heated pool you can see olive groves; ten minutes by car gets you to the Limski kanal, the Brijuni archipelago, and the truffle forests around Buzet. The result is relaxed Mediterranean elegance — quiet enough for a sabbatical, lively enough for a celebration.
homeLocation.p5: We host directly. Bookings made through ballenaandbeluga.com skip the platform fee and unlock concierge planning: airport transfer from Pula, private chef on request, daily cleaning on request, wedding and event coordination, baby cot and high chair, and 24/7 guest support in English, German, Italian and Croatian.
homeLocation.p6: If you have a question that isn't covered on the site, our FAQ answers the 13 most common ones in detail — from heated-pool season dates and pet policy to airport transfer and cancellation. For anything else, write to us and we usually reply within a few hours.

blog.post0Title: Why Istria Is Croatia's Best-Kept Secret for a Luxury Villa Holiday
blog.post0Excerpt: Discover why Istria — Croatia's green peninsula — is the ultimate destination for a private luxury villa escape, from truffle forests to medieval villages.
blog.post0Meta: Discover why Istria — Croatia's green peninsula — is the ultimate destination for a private luxury villa escape, from truffle forests to medieval villages.
blog.post0Intro: When most people think of Croatia, they picture Dubrovnik's terracotta rooftops or Split's bustling waterfront. And while those destinations deserve every bit of their fame, seasoned travelers know that the real magic lies further north — on the Istrian peninsula, where rolling green hills meet the Adriatic, and where luxury feels less like a production and more like a way of life.
blog.post0H1: A Peninsula That Has It All
blog.post0P1: Istria sits at Croatia's northwestern tip, just a short drive from Italy and Slovenia. It's often compared to Tuscany, and for good reason: the landscape is dotted with hilltop villages, ancient olive groves, and vineyards producing world-class Malvazija and Teran wines. But unlike Tuscany, Istria hasn't been overwhelmed by mass tourism. The pace here is slower, the crowds are thinner, and the experiences feel personal.
blog.post0P1b: The coastline offers crystal-clear waters and hidden coves, while the interior is home to dense oak forests where some of the world's finest truffles are hunted each autumn. It's the kind of place where you can spend the morning swimming in the Adriatic and the afternoon tasting olive oil at a family estate that's been pressing for generations.
blog.post0P2: At the heart of Istria's interior lies Svetvincenat, a medieval village centered around the stunning Morosini-Grimani castle. The castle's courtyard hosts summer concerts and cultural events, yet the village itself remains wonderfully untouched by mainstream tourism.
blog.post0P2b: This is where Villa Ballena and Villa Beluga are located — just 550 meters from the castle walls, yet completely private and secluded. It's the perfect base for exploring Istria: Rovinj is 23 kilometers away, Pula's Roman amphitheater is a 30-minute drive, and the hilltop artists' village of Groznjan is less than an hour north.
blog.post0H3: Why a Private Villa Beats a Hotel
blog.post0P3: Istria's charm is best experienced on your own terms. A private villa gives you something no hotel can: the freedom to wake up without a schedule, to have breakfast on your terrace in your bathrobe, to let the kids run wild in a fenced garden while you take a slow morning by the pool.
blog.post0P3b: At a luxury villa, there are no shared lobbies, no fighting for sun loungers, no restaurant reservations to worry about. You get a fully equipped kitchen for those evenings when you'd rather cook with fresh market ingredients than eat out. You get a private pool that's heated and ready whenever you are. And you get the kind of space — both physical and mental — that makes a holiday feel like a genuine reset.
blog.post0P4: No article about Istria would be complete without mentioning the food. This region punches far above its weight gastronomically. Fresh truffles — both black and the prized white variety — are shaved generously over handmade pasta, eggs, and beef carpaccio. Local olive oils regularly win international awards. The seafood is pulled from the Adriatic daily, and the wine scene is evolving rapidly, with young winemakers blending tradition and experimentation.
blog.post0P4b: Many villa guests find that their most memorable moments happen around the table: a private truffle dinner under the stars, a cooking class where you learn to make fuzi pasta from scratch, or simply a long evening BBQ on the terrace with a bottle of Kozlovic Malvazija.
blog.post0P5: Istria's season runs from May through October, with each period offering something different. Late May and June bring warm days, fewer crowds, and wildflowers covering the countryside. July and August are peak summer — perfect for families who want long pool days and beach excursions. September is arguably the most magical month: the light turns golden, the truffle season begins, and the grape harvest fills the air with celebration.
blog.post0P5b: Whichever month you choose, Istria rewards you with the kind of holiday that stays with you long after you've returned home — the kind where you find yourself, months later, still thinking about that sunset, that wine, that perfect evening on the terrace.
blog.post1Title: A Food Lover's Guide to Istria: Truffles, Olive Oil, and the Best Meal You've Never Had
blog.post1Excerpt: Explore Istria's extraordinary food scene — from world-class truffles and award-winning olive oils to family-run konobas serving recipes passed down for generations.
blog.post1Meta: Explore Istria's extraordinary food scene — from world-class truffles and award-winning olive oils to family-run konobas serving recipes passed down for generations.
blog.post1Intro: There's a running joke among Istrians: people come for the coast and stay for the food. It's not far from the truth. This small peninsula in northwestern Croatia has quietly built one of Europe's most exciting food scenes — not through Michelin-starred restaurants or celebrity chefs, but through something more enduring: a deep, almost stubborn connection to the land and its seasons.
blog.post1H1: The Truffle Capital of the Mediterranean
blog.post1P1: Istria is one of the few places in the world where both black and white truffles grow in abundance. The dense oak forests around the Mirna river valley — particularly near Motovun and Livade — produce white truffles that rival anything coming out of Alba, Italy, often at a fraction of the price.
blog.post1P1b: Black truffles are available year-round, but the white truffle season from September through December is when Istria truly comes alive. Local hunters head into the forests before dawn with their trained dogs, returning with treasures that end up shaved over everything from scrambled eggs to beef carpaccio to homemade fuzi pasta.
blog.post1P1c: The best way to experience this is firsthand. Truffle hunting excursions let you join a local guide and their dog in the forest, then sit down to a multi-course truffle meal afterward. It's the kind of experience that makes you realize truffles aren't just an ingredient — in Istria, they're a way of life.
blog.post1H2: Olive Oil That Wins World Championships
blog.post1P2: If you think olive oil is just olive oil, Istria will change your mind. This region consistently produces some of the highest-rated extra virgin olive oils on the planet. In Flos Olei, the world's most authoritative olive oil guide, Istria regularly places more oils per square kilometer than any other region.
blog.post1P2b: The secret lies in the varieties — Buza, Istarska Bjelica, and Leccino — grown in the peninsula's unique microclimate of warm Mediterranean air and cool continental breezes. The result is oil with remarkable complexity: grassy, peppery, sometimes almost artichoke-like, and always intensely fresh.
blog.post1P2c: Visiting a family-owned olive estate is one of Istria's most intimate experiences. You'll learn to taste oil properly (yes, there's a technique), understand the difference between early and late harvest, and leave with bottles you'll ration carefully once you're home.
blog.post1P3: Forget fine dining — the heart of Istrian gastronomy lives in the konoba. These rustic, family-run taverns serve the kind of food that doesn't need a menu to impress: slow-cooked dishes passed down through generations, using whatever the land and sea provide that day.
blog.post1P3b: Expect handmade pasta in several forms — fuzi (rolled quills), pljukanci (hand-torn strips), and gnocchi made with local potatoes. These come topped with game ragu, truffle sauce, or simple tomato and basil. The meat dishes are memorable too, especially lamb or beef cooked under a peka — a domed iron lid covered in hot coals that slow-roasts everything to extraordinary tenderness.
blog.post1P3c: A meal at a good konoba rarely costs more than 25 to 35 euros per person, including wine. And the wine will be excellent.
blog.post1P4: Istrian wine has been flying under the radar for too long, but that's changing fast. The region's signature grape is Malvazija Istarska — a white variety that produces wines ranging from light and mineral to rich and barrel-aged. In skilled hands, Malvazija can stand alongside the best white wines of Friuli or Burgundy.
blog.post1P4b: On the red side, Teran (related to Refosco) delivers earthy, tannic wines that pair beautifully with the local cured meats and aged cheeses. And a growing number of young winemakers are experimenting with orange wines, natural fermentation, and amphora aging — pushing Istria's wine scene in exciting new directions.
blog.post1P4c: Many wineries welcome visitors for tastings, often paired with prosciutto, cheese, and olive oil from neighboring farms. Estates like Kozlovic, Clai, Coronica, and Kabola are all within easy driving distance of Svetvincenat.
blog.post1H5: The Markets and the Ritual of Shopping
blog.post1P5: In Istria, food shopping isn't an errand — it's a social event. The morning markets in towns like Rovinj, Pula, and Vodnjan overflow with seasonal produce: wild asparagus in spring, figs and tomatoes in summer, porcini mushrooms and chestnuts in autumn.
blog.post1P5b: Vendors here aren't anonymous — they're farmers who grew what they're selling, often just hours before. You'll find homemade cheese, honey from local beekeepers, jars of fig jam, and dried herbs that smell like the Istrian hillside. A morning spent at the Rovinj market, followed by lunch at a nearby konoba, is one of the simplest and most satisfying days you can have in this part of the world.
blog.post1P6: The best advice for anyone visiting Istria is simple: eat where the locals eat, buy what the season offers, and never rush a meal. This is a place where lunch can last two hours and nobody apologizes for it, where the waiter might bring you something that isn't on the menu because it was just caught or just picked, and where the bill at the end of the evening will make you wonder how something this good can cost this little.
blog.post1P6b: Istria doesn't shout about its food. It doesn't need to. One meal is usually enough to understand why people keep coming back.
blog.post2Title: Beyond the Villa: 10 Unforgettable Experiences in Istria
blog.post2Excerpt: From truffle hunting to Roman amphitheaters — the best things to do near Svetvincenat, Istria, all within an hour of your luxury villa.
blog.post2Meta: From truffle hunting to Roman amphitheaters — the best things to do near Svetvincenat, Istria, all within an hour of your luxury villa.
blog.post2Intro: A great villa holiday needs a great destination — and Istria delivers on every front. From your base in Svetvincenat, some of Croatia's most rewarding experiences are less than an hour away. Whether you're a foodie, a history lover, a nature seeker, or traveling with kids who need constant stimulation, here are ten experiences that will make your Istrian holiday unforgettable.
blog.post2H1: 1. Truffle Hunting in the Motovun Forest
blog.post2P1: Istria is one of the world's premier truffle regions, and the forests around Motovun are where the magic happens. Join a local hunter and their trained dogs for a morning walk through ancient oak woods, then sit down to a truffle-heavy lunch that will redefine your understanding of this ingredient. Available year-round, though autumn is the season for the prized white truffle.
blog.post2H2: 2. Wine Tasting at Istria's Top Wineries
blog.post2P2: Istrian wine has been quietly earning international recognition. Malvazija — the region's signature white grape — produces wines that range from crisp and mineral to rich and oak-aged. Visit estates like Kozlovic, Clai, or Coronica for guided tastings that pair beautifully with local cheese and prosciutto. Most wineries are within 30 minutes of Svetvincenat.
blog.post2P3: Just 23 kilometers away, Rovinj is one of the Mediterranean's most photogenic towns. Its pastel-colored houses tumble down a hillside into the harbor, crowned by the Church of St. Euphemia. Wander the narrow cobblestone streets, browse the art galleries, eat fresh fish at the harbor, and watch the sunset from one of the rocky beaches along the Zlatni Rt forest park.
blog.post2P4: The Arena in Pula is one of the best-preserved Roman amphitheaters in the world — and at 27 kilometers from your villa, it makes for an easy half-day trip. Built in the 1st century AD, it once held 23,000 spectators. Today it hosts summer concerts and film festivals. The underground chambers, where gladiators once waited, now house a fascinating exhibition on Roman-era olive oil and wine production.
blog.post2P5: Istrian olive oils consistently rank among the world's best, and visiting a family-owned estate is one of the region's most intimate experiences. Learn about the harvest, the pressing process, and the difference between Buza, Istarska Bjelica, and Leccino varieties. Most tastings include fresh bread, local cheese, and views over endless olive groves. About 20 minutes from Svetvincenat.
blog.post2P6: This archipelago off the coast near Fazana (26 km away) was once Tito's private retreat and is now a national park. Take the ferry across, then explore by electric train or bicycle. You'll find Roman ruins, a safari park with exotic animals, and some of the most pristine swimming spots on the Adriatic. A full-day excursion that's especially rewarding for families.
blog.post2H7: 7. The Hilltop Villages: Motovun and Groznjan
blog.post2P7: Istria's interior is dotted with medieval hilltop towns that look like they belong in a film. Motovun sits dramatically above the Mirna river valley and hosts a famous film festival each summer. Groznjan, known as the 'artists' town,' is filled with galleries, studios, and jazz music drifting from open windows. Both are about 45 minutes north of Svetvincenat and can easily be combined into a single afternoon drive.
blog.post2P8: The nearest beaches are 19 to 23 kilometers away, along the coast between Bale, Fazana, and Rovinj. Istria's beaches tend to be rocky rather than sandy — which means the water is impossibly clear. Pack a snorkel, find a quiet cove, and spend the afternoon doing nothing at all. For families, the beaches near Fazana offer gentler entry points and nearby restaurants for when hunger strikes.
blog.post2H9: 9. Cooking Class: Istrian Fuzi and More
blog.post2P9: One of the best souvenirs from any trip is a recipe you can recreate at home. Book a private cooking class and learn to make fuzi (Istria's signature hand-rolled pasta), pair it with fresh truffles, and finish with a fritule dessert. Classes are typically held at local agriturismos and include all the wine you can reasonably drink while operating a pasta roller.
blog.post2H10: 10. Kastel Morosini-Grimani — Steps from Your Door
blog.post2P10: You don't even need to get in the car for this one. The medieval castle of Morosini-Grimani is just 550 meters from the villas, in the center of Svetvincenat. Its beautifully preserved courtyard hosts summer concerts, theater performances, and cultural events throughout the season. On a quiet evening, walk over, grab a coffee at one of the village's small cafes, and soak in the atmosphere of a place where the 15th century feels remarkably close.
blog.post2Outro: The best part about all these experiences? Your villa team can arrange any of them for you — from booking truffle hunts to recommending the best beach for your family. All you need to do is show up and enjoy.

about.title: Our Story
about.subtitle: Two villas, one philosophy
about.story: Villa Ballena and Villa Beluga were born from a deep love for Istria — its rolling hills, truffle forests, and sun-drenched coastline. Built in 2021 in the heart of Svetvinčenat, just steps from a medieval castle, these two sister villas represent our vision of what a perfect Mediterranean retreat should be: private, beautifully designed, and deeply connected to the land.
about.philosophy: We believe luxury should feel effortless. No check-in desks, no rigid schedules, no compromise. Just thoughtfully designed spaces, warm hospitality, and the freedom to create your own rhythm. Whether you're here for a quiet wellness escape or a lively family celebration, we want you to feel at home — in the most extraordinary way.
about.value1Desc: Your own fenced grounds, private pool, and secluded terrace. No shared lobbies, no neighbors peering over. Just your family and the Istrian sky.
about.value2Desc: Every detail is intentional. From the underfloor heating to the biological pool water, our villas blend contemporary aesthetics with functional luxury.
about.value3Desc: We are rooted in Istria. We know the truffle hunters, the winemakers, the fishermen. Every experience we recommend is one we have lived ourselves.
about.value4Desc: No rigid schedules or impersonal service. Just attentive, warm support when you need it and complete freedom when you do not.
about.ctaBody: Whether you seek a quiet wellness retreat or a lively family celebration, Villa Ballena and Villa Beluga await you in the heart of Istria.
